statement: The source adaptive contour/profile construction supplies an actual arithmetic upper approximant where the Observatory's earlier fixed-cluster polynomial Gram route stopped at an unproved growing-cluster transfer.
compatible_assumptions: RH aligns all roots; arbitrary complex integer Dirichlet coefficients of length<=N; full Cauchy boundary norm; fixed tiny contour mesh; multiplicities unrestricted and no growing inverse Gram matrix. This is an alternative proof route, not a claim that the earlier missing Gram lemma now follows.
new_claim_suggested: Investigate a fixed-degree L-function analog only after explicitly verifying small-window counts, reciprocal contours, Dirichlet synthesis and its pole/anchor structure.
already_proved: Source Theorem1 scoped reconstruction and fixed-Laurent qualification; published Burnol lower bound matches integer cutoff exactly. Source credit retained.
conjectural_or_unresolved: Effective finite-N constants, independent external expert assessment, exact publication priority, prefix lower bound and finite-off-line extensions; transfer beyond zeta not proved.
next_precise_step: Quantify the finite-Y local error and tail under explicit certified reciprocal bounds; independently reconstruct compact-jet prefix lower bound from paper47.
potential_counterexamples: Off-line poles destroy unit-modulus convolution phases. Pole data alone can hide an entire remainder. Summability of individual norms is neither implied nor needed. A continuous correction without quadrature need not lie in zeta D_N.
tests: Independent full main-proof reconstructions, exact norm/cutoff check against Burnol, termwise local repair, rational cutoff exponent and profile controls; infinite assertions rest on analytic proofs.
significance: Supports an RH-only optimized rate in a primary manuscript with fewer hypotheses than the inspected BCF prescribed-array theorem; no independent publication or discovery claim.
difficulty: Substantial analytic contour, growing multiplicity and arithmetic approximation argument.
